New machine. Its objects are: virosal, tebodal, vodilik, tevasar, muvive, degesu.
You have 4 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by placing half the objects on the machine to narrow down where the nexioms are.

TEST: virosal, tebodal, vodilik
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

The machine stayed dark with virosal, tebodal and vodilik. If any single nexiom is enough to light it, both nexioms must be among tevasar, muvive and degesu. That rule isn't confirmed yet: it might need both nexioms together. I'll test tevasar on its own to narrow this down.

TEST: tevasar
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Two rules are still possible. The machine might light whenever at least one nexiom is on it, or it might need both nexioms together.

- **If one nexiom is enough:** the first dark result puts both nexioms among tevasar, muvive and degesu. The second dark result rules out tevasar, so the nexioms would be muvive and degesu.
- **If both are needed:** the dark results only tell me the nexioms are not both among virosal, tebodal and vodilik.

Testing muvive and degesu together should settle a lot. If it lights, they are the nexioms under either rule. If it stays dark, the "one is enough" rule is ruled out and I'll use my last test to narrow down the remaining pairs.

TEST: muvive, degesu
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

The machine has stayed dark three times, so "one nexiom is enough" is ruled out. Only stricter rules remain, such as needing both nexioms together.

- **If both are needed:** the nexioms are not both in {virosal, tebodal, vodilik}, and they are not muvive and degesu. That leaves 11 possible pairs: any one of virosal, tebodal or vodilik with any one of tevasar, muvive or degesu (9 pairs), plus tevasar–muvive and tevasar–degesu.
- **Odds of success:** one yes/no test can't separate 11 pairs. I can't guarantee the right answer, so I'll use this test to cut the candidates roughly in half.

This test lights only if the pair is one of five: virosal–tevasar, virosal–muvive, tebodal–tevasar, tebodal–muvive or tevasar–muvive. If it stays dark, six candidates remain.

TEST: virosal, tebodal, tevasar, muvive
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

I can't be sure of this answer. One yes/no test couldn't separate the 11 pairs that were left, and the result below is still only a best guess.

**Rule:** every test stayed dark, so "one nexiom is enough" is ruled out. The likeliest rule is that both nexioms must be on the machine together.

**Remaining pairs under that rule:** the last test removes the five pairs it contained, leaving six:
- vodilik–tevasar
- vodilik–muvive
- vodilik–degesu
- virosal–degesu
- tebodal–degesu
- tevasar–degesu

**Choice:** vodilik and degesu each appear in several of these, so vodilik–degesu is the pair I pick. That gives about a one-in-six chance if the rule is "both needed".

**Another possibility:** if the machine instead lights only when exactly one nexiom is present, the four results point to virosal–tebodal.

ANSWER: nexioms = vodilik, degesu
One last question. If only degesu were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

**No**, most likely. Every rule consistent with the four dark results predicts that degesu alone would not light the machine:

- **Both nexioms needed:** a single object can never light it, whether or not degesu is a nexiom.
- **Exactly one nexiom needed:** degesu cannot be a nexiom.
  - If degesu were a nexiom and muvive were not, the muvive–degesu test held exactly one nexiom and would have lit.
  - If both muvive and degesu were nexioms, the last test held only muvive, exactly one, and would have lit.
  - Both tests stayed dark, so under this rule degesu is not a nexiom and would not light the machine alone.

I'm fairly confident in this, but it is not certain. A rule I haven't considered could still give a different result.

PROBE: no

Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

All four tests stayed dark, which points to a rule where the machine lights only when both nexioms are present. Under that rule, the nexioms are split, with one from donebus, muvize and pamogo and one from lopapes, kipeva and kadafok.

- **Test 4** stayed dark, so pamogo and kadafok are not the pair.

If the less likely rule holds instead (it lights only when exactly one nexiom is present), the pair would be donebus + muvize or lopapes + kipeva.

One last question. If only lopapes were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

- **Ruled out:** a rule where any single nexiom lights it. Test 2 had lopapes, kipeva and kadafok and stayed dark, so lopapes can't light it that way.

Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

The first test ruled out "any single nexiom lights the machine." Under that rule, both nexioms would be among kametik, rovavir and dulusis. The second test would then rule out kametik and rovavir, leaving only dulusis, which isn't enough for two. So the machine most likely lights only when both nexioms are present.

Under that rule, the pair can't be two of ladigus, mamatol and temigos, and it can't be kametik with rovavir. That leaves 11 possible pairs. With two tests left I can't separate all 11, so I'll split them as evenly as I can.

Testing ladigus, mamatol, kametik and dulusis would light the machine for 5 of the pairs. It would stay dark for the other 6.

TEST: ladigus, mamatol, kametik, dulusis
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

The third test lit up, so the pair is inside {ladigus, mamatol, kametik, dulusis}. It can't be ladigus with mamatol, because the first test would then have lit. That leaves five pairs: ladigus–kametik, ladigus–dulusis, mamatol–kametik, mamatol–dulusis and kametik–dulusis.

One test can't separate five pairs, so I'll split them 3 to 2. This assumes the machine needs both nexioms present, which the first two results strongly suggest. Testing ladigus, kametik and dulusis would light for three of the pairs: ladigus–kametik, ladigus–dulusis and kametik–dulusis. It would stay dark for mamatol–kametik and mamatol–dulusis.

TEST: ladigus, kametik, dulusis
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Assuming the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it, the results narrow it down this way:

- **Test 3** lit up, so both nexioms are among ladigus, mamatol, kametik and dulusis.
- **Test 1** stayed dark, so the pair isn't ladigus with mamatol.
- **Test 4** stayed dark, so the pair isn't any two of ladigus, kametik and dulusis.

That leaves two pairs: mamatol–kametik or mamatol–dulusis. Mamatol is a nexiom in both. Nothing separates kametik from dulusis, so the second object is a 50/50 guess, and I'm choosing dulusis.

This depends on the "both needed" rule. If the machine instead lit when exactly one nexiom is on it, the results would point to mamatol and temigos.

ANSWER: nexioms = mamatol, dulusis
One last question. If only dulusis were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

**No.** Under the rule I assumed, that the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it, a single object can never light it, whether or not dulusis is a nexiom.

The other rule that fits all four results is that the machine lights when exactly one nexiom is on it. Under that rule the nexioms would be mamatol and temigos, and dulusis is not one of them. So dulusis alone would still stay dark.

PROBE: no

New machine. Its objects are: dukofe, sotefe, gokifar, dopokar, regitis, kozumas.
You have 4 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects to narrow down where the nexioms are.

TEST: dukofe, sotefe, gokifar
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

No light from dukofe, sotefe and gokifar. If any single nexiom is enough to trigger the machine, both nexioms must be among the other three. If both nexioms are needed together, this only rules out both being in the first group. Testing the other three together will help separate these cases.

TEST: dopokar, regitis, kozumas
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

dukofe, sotefe and gokifar did not light the machine, but dopokar, regitis and kozumas did. This holds whether one nexiom is enough or both are needed. So both nexioms are very likely among dopokar, regitis and kozumas. Testing dopokar alone will show whether a single nexiom can light the machine, and if so, whether dopokar is one of them.

TEST: dopokar
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

The results so far narrow things down. The first group (dukofe, sotefe, gokifar) did not light the machine, but the second group (dopokar, regitis, kozumas) did, and dopokar alone did not.

**If one nexiom is enough to light the machine:**
- Neither nexiom can be in the first group.
- Dopokar is not a nexiom either.
- So the nexioms must be regitis and kozumas.

**If both nexioms are needed together:**
- Both must be in the second group, since only that group lit up.
- Dopokar alone would never light the machine under this rule, so test 3 tells us nothing here.
- The possible pairs are dopokar+regitis, dopokar+kozumas, or regitis+kozumas.

**If exactly one nexiom must be present:**
- The second group lit up, so it holds exactly one nexiom.
- That puts the other nexiom in the first group, which would then have lit up too.
- It didn't, so this rule is ruled out.

Testing regitis and kozumas together is the most useful last test.
- If it lights up, the answer is regitis + kozumas under either rule.
- If it doesn't, the rule must be "both needed", and the answer is either dopokar + regitis or dopokar + kozumas. I would have to guess between those two.

TEST: regitis, kozumas
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Regitis and kozumas together lit the machine, and that settles it under either rule.

- **If one nexiom is enough:** the earlier tests already left only regitis and kozumas. Group 1 (dukofe, sotefe, gokifar) did not light, and dopokar alone did not light.
- **If both nexioms are needed:** a two-object test can only light up if it holds both nexioms, so they must be regitis and kozumas.

The "exactly one nexiom" rule was already ruled out by the first two tests.

ANSWER: nexioms = regitis, kozumas
One last question. If only kozumas were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

I can't be sure, because my tests never separated the two possible rules.

- **If one nexiom is enough to light the machine:** kozumas alone would light it up.
- **If both nexioms are needed together:** kozumas alone would not light it up.

Every result fits both rules. Dopokar alone failed to light the machine, but it is not a nexiom, so that tells us nothing about a single nexiom. I never tested regitis or kozumas on its own, which is what would have settled it.

So my answer is close to a coin flip. I lean slightly towards "one nexiom is enough", since that seems the more natural way for a detector to work. This is a guess, not something the evidence shows.

PROBE: yes
